items.author: StephenBadger
items.body:
In graphiti_core/utils/maintenance/community_operations.py, the label_propagation function performs iterative community detection based on neighbor voting.

However, there is no hard limit on the number of iterations, and the loop is governed only by a convergence check (no_change).

If convergence is not reached — for example, in graphs with oscillating or ambiguous neighbor relationships — the loop may never terminate.

In my setup, where I am using Graphiti MCP to be the memory bank of an AI Agent for coding, while doing the original input of my code structure, the I kept getting this issue
items.title: Label Propagation Lacks Max Iteration Cap, Risking Infinite Loop on Non-Converging Graphs

On FalkorDB every `group_id` is a separate graph (multi-tenant), but the MCP server's `get_episodes` and `delete_episode` tools query whatever graph the shared driver happens to be bound to — `default_db` at startup, or the graph of the **last-written group** after any `add_episode` (which rebinds the driver via `self.driver = self.driver.clone(database=group_id)`). Neither tool routes to the graph of the requested group, so on FalkorDB they operate on the wrong graph and report data as missing that demonstrably exists.

`add_memory` returns `200` with a "queued for processing" message, after which the episode can be **discarded entirely** with no way for the caller to ever learn it. For a memory server this is silent data loss: the client believes the fact was stored, and nothing in the response, the tool result, or any queryable state says otherwise.

The trigger I hit was extraction output exceeding `max_tokens`, but the reporting gap is independent of the cause — anything that makes `queue_service` give up produces the same silence.

items.author: brentkearney
items.body:
## Environment

- **Graphiti version**: based on 0.29.3. Line numbers below are from a fork with unrelated local patches, so they may be off by a few lines from stock 0.29.3, but the code quoted is unmodified.
- **Database backend**: FalkorDB
- **LLM provider**: Google Gemini (small model used for the dedupe/contradiction judge)

## Problem

Saving a memory that merely *mentions* an entity can retire an unrelated, still-true fact about that entity. The retired fact stays in the graph but is stamped with an `invalid_at` date, so searches downrank or drop it and the knowledge is effectively gone
items.title: Bug: Edge invalidation searches the whole graph, so unrelated facts retire each other
